problem_text:
A manufacturing consortium aims to devise a resource‑conservation strategy to curtail raw material waste from several production lines. Initially, no efficiency improvements have been implemented.

The characteristics of each production line are as follows:
* For Line 1, waste coefficient is 2.69, output volume is 165.18.
* For Line 2, waste coefficient is 2.533, output volume is 196.707.
* For Line 3, waste coefficient is 1.937, output volume is 56.838.
* For Line 4, waste coefficient is 2.235, output volume is 79.067.
* For Line 5, waste coefficient is 2.915, output volume is 66.889.
* For Line 6, waste coefficient is 1.908, output volume is 208.415.
* For Line 7, waste coefficient is 2.425, output volume is 298.55.
* For Line 8, waste coefficient is 2.394, output volume is 219.228.
* For Line 9, waste coefficient is 2.903, output volume is 107.483.
* For Line 10, waste coefficient is 1.647, output volume is 128.933.

To reduce waste, several efficiency‑enhancing technologies are available, each offering a specific reduction in material loss:
* Technology1 reduces waste by 14%
* Technology2 reduces waste by 49%
* Technology3 reduces waste by 89%
* Technology4 reduces waste by 23%
* Technology5 reduces waste by 70%
* Technology6 reduces waste by 83%
* Technology7 reduces waste by 36%
* Technology8 reduces waste by 24%
* Technology9 reduces waste by 84%
* Technology10 reduces waste by 16%

Implementing a technology on a production line incurs an extra cost per unit of output. The cost matrix for all line–technology combinations is as follows:

| Line \ Technology | Tech1 | Tech2 | Tech3 | Tech4 | Tech5 | Tech6 | Tech7 | Tech8 | Tech9 | Tech10 |
|--|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|-|
| Line 1 | 100.546 | 77.172 | 179.92 | 61.124 | 189.952 | 139.79 | 182.886 | 104.81 | 47.937 | 149.732 |
| Line 2 | 175.821 | 49.288 | 48.526 | 57.442 | 127.533 | 39.639 | 30.271 | 184.836 | 138.404 | 136.051 |
| Line 3 | 126.627 | 155.206 | 112.88 | 18.03 | 101.635 | 127.927 | 103.545 | 197.219 | 180.43 | 175.066 |
| Line 4 | 103.253 | 197.035 | 184.041 | 63.251 | 52.198 | 119.566 | 20.288 | 161.861 | 100.881 | 112.746 |
| Line 5 | 105.47 | 84.806 | 140.404 | 43.212 | 195.536 | 142.666 | 97.413 | 140.95 | 12.246 | 50.043 |
| Line 6 | 120.392 | 71.833 | 126.428 | 59.343 | 114.227 | 55.056 | 99.556 | 126.486 | 79.526 | 104.766 |
| Line 7 | 50.001 | 143.135 | 80.739 | 172.322 | 63.13 | 44.179 | 34.916 | 119.42 | 53.428 | 28.975 |
| Line 8 | 61.29 | 54.803 | 92.122 | 82.368 | 37.71 | 192.238 | 38.414 | 163.077 | 43.555 | 104.924 |
| Line 9 | 199.157 | 171.384 | 108.231 | 146.906 | 159.213 | 67.006 | 116.806 | 117.889 | 85.696 | 141.203 |
| Line 10 | 21.407 | 164.625 | 100.542 | 129.674 | 95.472 | 73.585 | 78.583 | 116.467 | 187.05 | 58.966 |

The consortium must decide which technologies to deploy on each line (multiple technologies may be applied simultaneously to a single line, and a line may also remain partially unoptimized if needed). The objective is to guarantee that the total material waste is lowered by at least a fraction P = 0.21 of the baseline waste, while minimizing the overall implementation cost.
